requirements.statement: The adaptive-minimal-proof-testing behavior is defined in a canonical always-on rule (rules/) with a machine-checkable contract in rules/manifest.yaml (kind=invariant, trigger=always-load) and is enforced by a validator, not by prompts or optional skills.

The trigger model derives activation from changed scope, affected claims, affected dependencies, risk class, runtime surface, project test architecture, host capability and required evidence fidelity — never from keywords alone.

The proof-profile catalog supports evidence categories A–K (static/structural, unit/deterministic, contract/schema, integration, API/service, browser/UI, live runtime, security/isolation, performance/reliability, data/migration, packaging/installation) and eight default profiles (trivial/static, business logic, API/service, UI/browser, MCP/desktop/process/session, security/permissions, migration/data, performance/reliability) with automatic escalation and no silent downgrade.

The proof-selection engine selects the smallest proof set that can actually prove the claims: deterministic proof first, fidelity escalation only when the claim requires it; every selected proof records claim covered, proof identifier, sufficiency, environment, result, evidence path, limitations and escalation path; every omitted proof records category, reason, why omission is safe and the condition requiring escalation.

Live claims (browser, desktop, MCP availability/tools, handshake, process/window attribution, virtual desktop, focus, headed/visible mode, session persistence, reconnect, resource recreation, network/provider, host integration, real auth, real data-state) require real live proof; unit/fake evidence cannot replace live proof for a live claim; the smallest real provider with pinned versions is used; BLOCKED is reported when the environment capability is unavailable and UNSUPPORTED when the host cannot provide the seam.

Every proof result is classified as exactly one of PASS | PARTIAL | BLOCKED | UNSUPPORTED | PRE-EXISTING | NEEDS_USER; PASS requires sufficient fresh evidence; BLOCKED/UNSUPPORTED are never converted into PASS; failures cannot be hidden by deleting or weakening tests; the whole task cannot be PASS while a required claim remains unresolved.

The verification router emits a proof receipt containing task identity, repository, changed scope, claims, risks, selected proof profile, selected tests, omitted tests, omission reasons, escalation decisions, environment, results, evidence references and final status; the router works through CLI, North-Star runtime, plan/review/implementation flows, handoff/resume flows, MCP/provider flows and platform adapters.

The test-refactor policy is global: audit and coverage-map before changing tests; protected tests (security, authorization, data integrity, migration, concurrency, lifecycle, regression, user-visible behavior) are preserved; every removed/merged/rewritten/downgraded test is recorded; post-refactor proof set runs and behavior coverage before/after is compared; forbidden operations (delete-to-green, weakened assertions, live-to-fake without claim change, silent flaky skips, retry-masked failures, behavior-change-to-fit-tests, delete-without-mapping) are rejected.

Canonical schemas exist for behavior contract, trigger/activation contract, proof profile, claim-to-proof mapping, risk-to-proof escalation, omission reason, proof receipt and test-refactor matrix; schema validators pass on positive fixtures and reject negative fixtures.

Sixteen validation/eval cases (trivial change, backend logic, API authorization, schema migration, frontend/UI, browser interaction, MCP provider, desktop/window/focus, security/isolation, performance-sensitive, flaky/duplicate refactor, blocked live environment, project with no tests, over-broad suite, only live/browser tests, only unit tests for a live claim) each demonstrate correct trigger, correct proof profile, no unnecessary proof, required escalation, honest status classification, evidence receipt and no silent skip.

A read-only project audit covers agent-rules, ZaloAI-Ecommerce and pos-ops reporting test runners, test categories, baseline counts, slow suites, duplicate patterns, browser/live capability, CI commands, missing proof layers, recommended minimal proof profile and project-specific escalation rules; the audit does not modify those projects' test files.

Platform mirrors are reconciled: source rule, generated route, installed mirror, platform projection, hash, activation path and native host limitations; native activation is never claimed from static file presence; NATIVE_UNVERIFIED is reported when activation is not proven.

Documentation defines the global always-on behavior (rule file, manifest contract, docs); the behavior is implemented in canonical behavior/verification layers, not only documented; a dedicated branch is committed and pushed after validation; the owner-managed Documents residual is untouched.
